name: Question 2
problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{yx}{{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}}
$$
worked_solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{yx}{{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{(vx)x}{(vx)^{2}+{x}^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{v{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}({v}^{2}+1)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v}{{v}^{2}+1}-v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v-{v}^{3}-v}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{-{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{{v}^{2}+1}{{v}^{3}}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{v}^{2}+1}{{v}^{3}}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{{v}^{3}})\,\text{d}v & =-\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|v|-\frac{1}{2{v}^{2}} & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+{C}_{1} \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡|v|-\frac{1}{{v}^{2}} & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2{C}_{1} \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡|v|-\frac{1}{{v}^{2}} & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we introduced $C=2{C}_{1}.$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{y}{x}|-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}} & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{y}{x}|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}} & =C \\ 2\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}} & =C\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

With y=v(x)x, we have: dydx=xdvdx+vddx(x)=xdvdx+v

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives: dydx=yxy2+x2xdvdx+v=(vx)x(vx)2+x2xdvdx+v=vx2x2(v2+1)xdvdx=vv2+1−vxdvdx=v−v3−vv2+1xdvdx=−v3v2+1v2+1v3dvdx=−1x

Integrating both sides with respect to x, we obtain: ∫v2+1v3dvdxdx=−∫1xdx∫(1v+1v3)dv=−∫1xdxln⁡|v|−12v2=−ln⁡|x|+C12ln⁡|v|−1v2=−2ln⁡|x|+2C12ln⁡|v|−1v2=−2ln⁡|x|+C

Notice that we introduced C=2C1.

From the transformation y=vx, we get v=yx.

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain: 2ln⁡|yx|−x2y2=−2ln⁡|x|+C2ln⁡|yx|+2ln⁡|x|−x2y2=C2ln⁡|y|−x2y2=C
